title: GROUP BY and aggregates
objective: Aggregate functions summarize groups; LEFT JOIN plus COUNT(child.id) preserves a group with zero related rows. COUNT(*) counts outer rows, not existing children.
misconception: The starter counts the joined row, losing the difference between an empty project and a project with one task.
acceptance: SQL SUM skips NULL values; COALESCE changes an empty sum into zero. Explain why WHERE child.status = ... would turn a LEFT JOIN into an effective INNER JOIN.
securityBoundary: COUNT(*) returns one for the unmatched outer row, so it does not mean one task exists.
